text:
ravi: Heads-up — customer Pecan Health flagged duplication of small numeric tokens after we onboarded their LoRA into semantix-7b and ran 4-bit quant.
emily: Can you paste an example?
ravi: Example they sent: "Invoice 000712 completed on 2024-02-15" -> model: "Invoice 000712 000712 completed on 2024-02-15"
noah: I started a small diagnostic sweep comparing float16 vs int4/awq across their sample set (n=500). Float16 dup ~0.2%, awq-4bit ~2.4%.
tara: Did we use pecan-v2 tokenizer or generic? Customer uses pecan-v2 everywhere.
noah: Default run used HF-generic. Re-ran with pecan-v2 and duplication dropped to 0.6%. So tokenizer mismatch is a big factor.
emily: But still higher than float16. Any kernel differences?
noah: Yep. Quick matrix:
- awq-native + pecan-v2 = 0.6%
- ggml-smooth + pecan-v2 = 0.15%
- awq-native + hf-generic = 2.4%
- ggml-smooth + hf-generic = 1.2%

So tokenizer alignment reduces it a lot, kernel choice further matters.
infra-bot: Diagnostic job 1751245000-diagnostics started on dedicated-gpu-5. Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/1751245000/logs
ravi: Hypothesis: tokenizer causes token boundary splits that interact poorly with AWQ scaling in attention, leading to repeated generation of short numeric tokens.
tara: Could be prefix cache handling too. Try with --disable-prefix-cache for a run.
noah: Ran that: awq-native + pecan-v2 + --disable-prefix-cache => 0.2% duplicates. ggml-smooth unchanged. So prefix caching+awq is the extra multiplier.
emily: Nice triage. Action list: (1) recommend customer set tokenizer=pecan-v2 in their integration; (2) set routing to ggml-smooth kernel for this LoRA as a temporary mitigation; (3) add a quick-eval CI test checking numeric-token repeat rate < 0.5% on representative invoices.
ravi: I'll draft the customer message: short note explaining workaround + ETA for kernel fix.
tara: I'll open an infra ticket to investigate AWQ prefix-cache scaling math (link in ticket).
infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-1129 — awq-prefix-cache-scaling.
noah: Saved the eval artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/1751245000/pecan-eval.tgz
emily: I'll add a tiny onboarding test to the LoRA repo that runs 40 invoice prompts and asserts no repeated numeric substrings > 0.5%.
ravi: Thanks all. If we want to be conservative, toggle default kernel for semantix-7b:loRA-pecan to ggml-smooth until INFRA-1129 done. :thumbsup:
